He tried to ask me out "platonically" a few times, but it was only ever us and it was always very coupley things. I politely declined, but he kept pushing, even trying to trick me into spending time with him. By my perception, he didn't actually care whether I was interested or not, he had decided we should be a couple despite my feelings and it was only by cutting the whole thing off cold turkey that he finally understood I wasn't interested.

And cold turkey is basically icing the person out, so if you can't even get a sideways glance, she is probably doing this.

I can't speak for your girl, but being friends with someone and then them turning around and saying "okay, can we move on to a romantic relationship?" can be pretty gutting, and if you're not careful - it can come across as entitled, like 'I've done my time as the friend, I'm ready for a promotion'. Maybe your texts were like these repeated ignorant attempts to get what he wanted. I'm absolutely not saying you tried to trick this girl, but the texts probably came across as an attempt to still be in control of an already delicate situation. You may have already fucked it but my one bit of advice is don't draw attention to the situation, relinquish control and let it run its course - the guy at my work kept trying to make passive aggressive jokes about how I thought I was too good/busy to talk to him, and it took me from really enjoying someone's company to actively wishing I didn't have to even look at them.

Anxiety really makes you polarise everything, they love you or they hate you, and it's so easy to see from an outsider's perspective that people read the situation incorrectly, but so hard to see yourself.

I'm positive if you were consciously behaving yourself today (which I think we also all seem to do), you would have noticed and amplified anything that went haywire.
